step: ROADMAP S2 (release acceptance, an open item; the model killing Night 7 nights the phone wins)
claimLevel: MODEL_ONLY replays over DEVICE_MEASURED clocks, landings and outcomes
exploratory: A sweep run after the 0/20 night's replay lost its glitch view in cycle 3; it tests no predeclared rule. Its bound is used, named, in the superseding 10/20 seed-scan predeclaration.
question: How late after its send can a contact's release land for the model to play a phone-won night the way the phone played it?

reading.zeroOfTwenty: On the 0/20 night (seed 23712, read off the static) the model dies to the Puppet at release latencies of 60 ms and more (at the press's 85.5 ms, 54.5 s in): a monitor still held when its raise completes is read again (Office g618/g619, contact-input.ts heldDropTouch) and drops the glitch view, so the box drains. At 50 ms and less it reaches 6 AM, as the phone did.
reading.fullSix: On full-06 at 10/20 (its measured seed 47593) the model died inside the office at 378.3 s at the press's 81.6 ms and at 70 ms; at 60 ms and less it reaches 6 AM, as the phone did. Its window agreement does not change (16 of 42, first disagreement at window 6): the release explains the outcome gap of this night, not its encounter divergence.
reading.bound: Both nights admit releases at 50 ms and less after the send, and neither admits the press's own latency. With the input-registration record's hall flash ending 3-5 updates before a release landed at 81.6 ms (docs/evidence/full06-input-registration-20260928.json), a release lands about 15-30 ms after its send: 50-70 ms sooner than a press.
reading.consequence: Every encounter replay that lands releases at the press latency (the landed variant) carries spurious held-contact drops; S2's "the model kills Night 7 nights the phone wins" is at least partly this. The 10/20 seed-scan predeclaration is superseded before its night to land releases at 20 ms.
